To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the learning ability of D. melanogaster decreases with aging, but the extinction rate does not change with age.

(1) acquisition of conditioned suppression of the probocsis-extension response in D. melanogaster flies is faster and more effective in young animals than in middle-aged and old animals, and (2) the extinction of the response is delayed in old flies.

1) acquisition of conditioned suppression was faster in young than in old flies; 2) acquisition of conditioned extinction was faster in middle-aged than in old flies, and 3) extinction of conditioned suppression was slower in old than in middle-aged and young flies.

the effects of age on the acquisition and extinction of a simple conditioned response in Drosophila.
the effects of aging on acquisition and extinction of a conditioned response in Drosophila.
the study of the age-related changes in the inhibitory conditioning of an appetitive reflex in Drosophila.
